use_case: UC1 - Air quality and traffic: explaining poor-air days and warning clinic patients a day ahead (Valdena Civic Health Office, IT; as of 2026-10-15)
objective_summary: Decide whether the poor-air-day warning method can be prototyped now on public hourly Italian air-quality readings (2004-03-10 to 2005-04-04), and whether the city's own two-year production data (2024-2025) covers air quality, traffic and daily district-level respiratory clinic counts at the needed grain. Also identify data that cannot be used and the red flags to resolve before profiling.

need_plans.interpretation: Hourly concentrations of NO2 and/or PM2.5 (and ideally PM10/O3) from fixed urban monitoring stations in Italy, covering the prototype window 2004-03-10 to 2005-04-04 and the production window 2024-01-01 to 2025-12-31 from the city's own station network. Must carry station id, pollutant, timestamp, unit and validity flag.
internal_queries: hourly air quality station readings NO2 PM2.5 Valdena
city air monitoring station data request status
ARPA station feed NO2 PM10 hourly
air quality station register and pollutant codes
external_data_hints: Italian regional environmental agency (ARPA) or national environmental body open-data portal, hourly station readings for an urban station in the Po Valley or another northern Italian city, 2004-03 to 2005-04; check the station actually has NO2/PM2.5 in that period (PM2.5 was not routinely measured at all stations in 2004).

Open-data portal of a northern Italian municipality or region with hourly historical archives; confirm licence on the source page before use (open-data policy: prototyping only without Legal sign-off).
acceptance_criteria: Hourly grain (no coarser aggregation) across the full prototype window with fewer than an agreed share of gaps, stated per pollutant
Station location (lat/long or municipality) recorded so that it can be matched to weather and traffic
Pollutant units and calibration/validation status documented
Licence or terms stated on the source page and compatible with prototyping; production use flagged for Legal sign-off
Production window: city station data delivered for 2024-01-01 to 2025-12-31 at hourly grain
likely_pitfalls: No register entry covers air quality: the prototype dataset must be found and approved by a human before use
PM2.5 coverage in 2004-2005 is sparse; NO2 may be the only pollutant with full coverage
Station codes or names change over time; a station may be relocated or renamed between 2005 and 2024
Mixed units (µg/m3 vs mg/m3) or local time vs UTC timestamps
Provisional values in the most recent months of an open-data feed are later revised
The city's own station data is still only requested: production window is not yet available

need_plans.interpretation: Hourly vehicle traffic counts or flow proxies on road links within a short distance of each monitoring station, for the production window 2024-01-01 to 2025-12-31. Not needed for the prototype window.
internal_queries: traffic counts hourly road sensors Valdena
traffic loop data by link id
vehicle flow near air monitoring station
external_data_hints: Municipal mobility or traffic-management office, or regional transport open-data portal, hourly vehicle counts for road links near the air-quality stations, 2024-2025; the grain must be hourly and the link must be near the station (state the distance).
acceptance_criteria: Hourly counts (or flow/speed) for 2024-01-01 to 2025-12-31 for at least the links near each station used in N1
Link-to-station mapping documented with distance
Counting method and gaps documented (sensor outages, changes of sensor)
Licence and ownership recorded; any city-owned data flagged for internal sign-off
likely_pitfalls: Traffic sensors often cover a few arterial roads only; a station may have no nearby counter
Sensor replacement or road works break series; counts may be in vehicles per day rather than per hour
Restrictions (ZTL, lockdowns) change traffic patterns in 2024-2025 and must be flagged as regime changes
No register source covers traffic; any external candidate needs a human decision

need_plans.interpretation: Hourly air temperature and relative humidity at or near the monitoring stations, covering both the prototype window (2004-03-10 to 2005-04-04) and the production window (2024-01-01 to 2025-12-31). Weather is used as a driver, so the source must be consistent across the two windows.
external_data_hints: If no city station is available for the prototype, use a reanalysis product (for example ERA5-based) at the client's coordinates; record that it is modelled, not observed. For production, prefer the city or regional meteorological station network if available.
acceptance_criteria: Hourly temperature_2m and relative humidity available for both windows at the chosen coordinates
Coordinates, time zone (UTC vs local) and model/station source recorded
Terms of the Open-Meteo licence checked for the intended use (register lists prototyping and production as approved purposes; confirm commercial-use terms at the licence URL)
Probe calls kept to a few days; no bulk download in discovery
likely_pitfalls: Vendor AtmosData Pro is expired (agreement ended 2025-12-31, key revoked 2026-01-01): do not use it for production or for the 2024-2025 window
Reanalysis grid cells (~10 km) smooth urban heat and humidity; comparisons with station data need a caveat
Local time vs UTC shifts the daily pattern and must be aligned with air-quality timestamps
Coordinates are an assumption (client city not named in any source) and must be confirmed by a human

need_plans.interpretation: Daily counts of respiratory clinic visits by district for 2024-01-01 to 2025-12-31, from the city's own clinic system, shared as aggregate counts only (no patient-level data).
internal_queries: respiratory clinic visits daily by district
clinic visit counts ICD respiratory codes
acceptance_criteria: Daily grain by district for every day of 2024-01-01 to 2025-12-31, with zero days explicit
Case definition for 'respiratory' (code list, e.g. ICD-10 J chapter) documented and agreed
Counts are aggregate with small-cell suppression rules documented
Data-sharing basis for the clinic-to-office transfer confirmed by a human (GDPR)
District code system mapped to a standard geography
likely_pitfalls: Clinic system migrations can split a series or change coding mid-period
Visit date vs registration date vs appointment date differ
Small districts produce small counts that may need suppression
Holidays and clinic closures produce zero or missing days that look like low demand

need_plans.interpretation: Event-level clinic visit records (one row per visit) for respiratory patients, for 2024-2025. Out of scope per the brief: individual patient records may not be used. Listed so that the decision is recorded.
acceptance_criteria: Recorded as excluded unless a human explicitly approves a lawful basis and a data-protection review; default is no use
If ever approved, no direct identifiers leave the clinic and the extract is pseudonymised with documented re-identification risk
likely_pitfalls: Brief says patient-level data is out of scope; using it anyway is a compliance breach
Pseudonymised patient ids can still be personal data under GDPR
Consent or legal basis for patient-level sharing is not evidenced in any source reviewed

need_plans.interpretation: National yearly context on deaths attributable to PM2.5 for Italy, annual grain, covering 2004-2005 (prototype) and 2024-2025 (production). Context only, not a model input.
internal_queries: deaths linked to particulate matter Italy
external_data_hints: National statistics office (ISTAT) or European Environment Agency / WHO published annual estimates of PM2.5-attributable deaths for Italy; annual grain, Italy-level, must cover 2004-2005 and 2024-2025 or state the gap. Beware estimates that are model-based and differ by method and year.
acceptance_criteria: Annual Italy-level figure for each year in the windows, or an explicit gap statement
Estimation method and version stated (model-based estimates are not observed counts)
Licence/terms of the publisher checked
likely_pitfalls: Attributable-death estimates are revised retrospectively; the vintage must be recorded
Different methods (GBD, EEA, WHO) give different numbers; do not mix them
Not a model input for hourly prediction

open_questions: Which Italian city should the client's coordinates and the prototype station be set in? No source names the city; the Open-Meteo call needs latitude/longitude and the assumption must be recorded in decisions.md.
Has the city's own air-quality station data request been sent, and what is the expected delivery date for 2024-2025?
Is there a city traffic-count source for 2024-2025 at hourly grain, and who owns it?
What is the lawful basis and data-sharing agreement for the district-level daily clinic counts (N4)?
Is a commercial-use licence needed for Open-Meteo in production, and has Legal reviewed it?
Which open-data air-quality dataset (for the prototype) has been approved by Legal for prototyping, and does its licence allow that use?
Is a replacement contract for the expired AtmosData Pro feed planned, and does the production model need it or can Open-Meteo or a city station replace it?
Which respiratory case definition (ICD-10 codes) does the clinic use?
